title: About.
lead: Backend and platform engineer in Gurgaon, India. Currently on a client platform team through Quess Corp, and looking for backend and DevOps roles.
paragraphs: I write Go, and I build the path that gets it to a cluster and keeps it there. Most of what I find interesting sits at the seam between those two things — a service is not finished when the handler returns the right JSON, it is finished when there is a repeatable way for it to reach production and an honest signal when it stops behaving.

The thing I keep coming back to is that infrastructure runs on claims nobody checks. A controller advertises self-healing. A chart declares a liveness probe. A pipeline says it blocks on vulnerabilities. In most repositories those are sentences, not results, because verifying them costs an afternoon and no reviewer is going to ask. The gap between a configured guarantee and a tested one is where outages live.

So the work on this site is written the other way round. Each project has a claim, a test I ran against it on purpose, the number that came back, and — the part that matters most — the list of cases the test does not cover. A benchmark without its boundaries is marketing. I would rather publish a smaller claim I can defend than a larger one I cannot.
Outside that: I read source when documentation disagrees with behaviour, which happens more than it should.
